ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is triangle DHG, and there is one pink tick mark on each of sides DH and HG, indicating DH = HG. Point F is on side DG, segment HF connects from H to DG, and there is a pink right-angle mark at F, indicating HF ⟂ DG. The dimension label beside side DG is 10. Then reason: Because DH = HG, triangle DHG is an isosceles triangle with H as the vertex and DG as the base. HF is the altitude drawn from vertex H of the isosceles triangle to base DG.
